newsitem.title: USA: US ADJ RETAIL SALES UP 0.9 PCT AUG 9 WK -- REDBOOK.
newsitem.headline: US ADJ RETAIL SALES UP 0.9 PCT AUG 9 WK -- REDBOOK.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.9 percent in the week ending August 9, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.

The index rose 8.6 percent compared with the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales also rose 8.6 percent in the week ended August 9 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
"We certainly are running ahead of trend line," Jay Meltzer, managing director of Redbook Research told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV). "They for one expect August to be a very good month."

Meltzer added that sales for stores with catalogue business have held up "remarkably well" during the United Parcel Service strike. Stores have contingency plans in effect, which have prevented adverse effects, he added.
Looking toward September, Meltzer told RFTV that purchases of warm-weather merchandise had simmered down.
"We think it's going to be a good back-to-school season," Meltzer said.
